title: A quotient by an element whose derivative is a unit along the quotient is regular
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a Jacobian criterion for hypersurfaces: if a regular ring admits a derivation sending an element to a unit of the quotient by that element, then the quotient is regular. The statement carries a slogan naming the criterion. The proof reduces to the local case with maximal ideal and residue field, where regularity of the quotient is equivalent to the element not lying in the square of the maximal ideal; were it to lie there, the Leibniz rule would force its derivative into the maximal ideal, contradicting the hypothesis.
